Package com.github.tommyettinger.cringe

Class PointHasher

java.lang.Object
com.github.tommyettinger.cringe.PointHasher
public final class PointHasher extends Object
A group of similar methods for getting hashes of points based on int coordinates in 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 dimensions and an int for state. This hash has high enough quality to be useful as a source of random numbers based on positions. The technique used here owes credit to Pelle Evensen for finding the significant quality increase from using multiple bitwise rotations XORed together. Credit also to Martin Roberts for discovering the connection between higher dimensional ranks and the appropriate numbers to gain similar qualities to adding the golden ratio mod 1 in 1D, using what had already been named "harmonious numbers." This class doesn't use the exact harmonious numbers (which are irrational numbers), but instead takes 2 to the 22 divided by that harmonious number and finds the next probable prime greater than or equal to that. Using primes may have advantages when there are lots of products being mixed like this.
This class offers both "hash" methods like hashAll(int, int, int) and "hashPrimed" methods like hashPrimedAll(int, int, int). The "hash" methods will almost always produce very different results when given very nearby points, because they internally multiply each parameter (other than s, the hash seed) by a different prime number per-axis and per-dimension. The "hashPrimed" methods assume that the non-s parameters are already multiples of different 21-bit prime numbers, and so they do not need to multiply internally. If you know what dimension and axis you're working with, and you would normally add 1 when working with a "hash" method, you can add a prime number from this class' constants, such as X2 or Z3, instead and use a "hashPrimed" method. This should be faster by avoiding quite a bit of multiplication in the long run. Multiplication tends to be substantially slower than addition with ints, so this can be a boost to performance when hashing points needs to be done many times per frame.
The only case where this can return different results on GWT than on a desktop or mobile JVM is when the inputs are GWT-specific out-of-range JS Numbers appearing to be ints. That's a problem with the input, rather than the algorithm.

    • HARMONIOUS_PRIMES

      public static final int[][] HARMONIOUS_PRIMES
      The prime constants declared in this class as X2, Z3, and so on, but organized so they are in arrays from 1D to 7D, with 1 item in the 1D array up to 7 items in the 7D array. This array should not be modified, but it isn't currently used internally, so nothing would break in this library if you did change it.

  • Method Details

    • hashAll

      public static int hashAll(int x, int s)
      A 32-bit point hash that smashes x into s using XOR and multiplications by harmonious numbers, then runs a simple unary hash on s and returns it. GWT-optimized. Inspired by Pelle Evensen's rrxmrrxmsx_0 unary hash, though this doesn't use its code or its full algorithm. The unary hash used here has been stripped down heavily, both for speed and because unless points are selected specifically to target flaws in the hash, it doesn't need the intense resistance to bad inputs that rrxmrrxmsx_0 has.
      Parameters:
      x - x position, as an int
      s - any int, a seed to be able to produce many hashes for a given point
      Returns:
      32-bit hash of the x point with the given state s

      A 32-bit point hash that smashes x, y, z, w, u, v, and m into s using XOR and multiplications by harmonious numbers, then runs a simple unary hash on s and returns it. GWT-optimized. Inspired by Pelle Evensen's rrxmrrxmsx_0 unary hash, though this doesn't use its code or its full algorithm. The unary hash used here has been stripped down heavily, both for speed and because unless points are selected specifically to target flaws in the hash, it doesn't need the intense resistance to bad inputs that rrxmrrxmsx_0 has.
      Parameters:
      x - x position, as an int
      y - y position, as an int
      z - z position, as an int
      w - w position, as an int
      u - u position, as an int
      v - v position, as an int
      m - m position, as an int
      s - any int, a seed to be able to produce many hashes for a given point
      Returns:
      32-bit hash of the x,y,z,w,u,v,m point with the given state s
